title: Rise of the Robots
subtitle: Technology and the Threat of a Jobless Future
pitch: A software entrepreneur argues that this time automation is different: machines are starting to do mental work, and many jobs may not come back.

chapters.g: Robots and software are spreading from factories into warehouses, restaurants and offices.
Wages stalled and job growth weakened even as productivity rose, which Ford reads as an early sign.

chapters.t: Information technology: an unprecedented force for disruption
chapters.g: Computing keeps getting better at an exponential rate, unlike most past technologies.
Writing, analysis, law and other knowledge work are increasingly automatable.
Online courses and automated grading could shake up universities.
Where AI might help or replace work in medicine, and why costs are hard to cut.

chapters.t: Consumers, limits to growth ... and crisis?
chapters.g: If incomes fall, who buys what the machines make.
A look at the bigger AI risks and hopes, from Kurzweil to Bostrom.
Ford's case for a basic income and other ways to share the gains.

ideas: Automation is now reaching cognitive work, not only manual work.
Productivity can rise while wages and jobs fall behind.
Mass unemployment could hurt demand and the whole economy.
A guaranteed basic income may be needed.

args.a: Machines will take many jobs faster than new ones appear.
args.c: Past waves of automation created more jobs than they destroyed, and employment stayed high after the book came out.

args.a: A basic income is the best response.
args.c: Others prefer wage subsidies, retraining or job guarantees, and worry about cost and incentives.

questions: Which tasks in your own job could software do today?
Would a basic income change how people find meaning in work?
Is the jobs problem a stepping stone to bigger AI risks, or a separate issue?

quiz.q: What kind of jobs does Ford say are newly at risk?
quiz.w: Software is starting to do mental work.
He argues for sharing the gains broadly.

o: If incomes fall, demand for goods may collapse
